meta.Zones covered: Garden & tree canopy (nadir) | pavilion structure (close-range oblique)
meta.Annotated videos: Two MP4 files in this folder, one per clip

headlineFindings: The two clips are very different in kind. Clip 1 is a conventional overhead garden survey; Clip 2 is a close-range oblique of a pavilion structure, flown a few metres from the wall. Read them separately - the area-based ground metrics only apply to Clip 1.

Clip 1's planting is in good condition: 75% green cover, healthy canopy and flowering shrubs, only 4.6% bare ground and a strong irrigation score of 93.5. This does not match the site note of widespread dry patches, which suggests the dry areas are elsewhere in the park than this clip covers.
Cleanliness is the weak point in Clip 1 at 30.7/100 - loose ground debris and leaf litter under the canopy, consistent with the site record of garbage and poor housekeeping.

Clip 2 is the evidence for 'infrastructure in poor condition'. The pavilion shows heavy damp staining down the stonework, peeling and blackened paint on the parapet, cracked render and a weathered downpipe. This is a visual record rather than a measurement - the detector has no class for paint failure or damp staining.
A bench is visible in use under the pavilion and was detected; 161 bench records across the survey.
Dry and dead vegetation appears in 306 records, mostly around the pavilion surrounds where the ground is bare and compacted.
Vehicles were detected inside the park boundary (4 records).

recommendations.Finding: The pavilion in Clip 2 shows heavy damp staining down the stonework, blackened and peeling paint on the parapet, and cracked render - matching the site record of infrastructure in poor condition.
recommendations.Recommended action: Commission a structural and damp survey of the pavilion. The staining pattern suggests a failed roof edge or blocked downpipe; repair the water path before redecorating, or the paint will fail again.

recommendations.Finding: Cleanliness in the garden zone is 30.7/100, the weakest score in this park, driven by loose ground debris and leaf litter under the canopy.
recommendations.Recommended action: Increase sweeping frequency under the tree canopy; add or reposition bins in the garden zone.

recommendations.Finding: Ground around the pavilion is bare and compacted (27.7% of frame) with dry vegetation, in contrast to the healthy garden zone.
recommendations.Recommended action: Reinstate ground cover in the pavilion surrounds; relieve compaction from foot traffic and provide a defined paved apron where desire lines have formed.

recommendations.Finding: Vehicles were detected inside the park boundary.
recommendations.Recommended action: Confirm whether the movements are authorised; otherwise enforce vehicle restrictions.

recommendations.Finding: The garden zone is in good condition - 75% green cover, healthy flowering canopy and shrubs, irrigation score 93.5.
recommendations.Recommended action: Maintain the current planting regime in this zone.

recommendations.Finding: The site record describes widespread dry patches and poor lawn across this park, but Clip 1 shows healthy planting and only 4.6% bare ground. The two clips do not cover the open lawn areas where those defects were observed.
recommendations.Recommended action: Fly the open lawn and pathway areas of R Block to capture the dry-patch evidence; the current pair of clips under-represents the park's condition.

recommendations.Finding: Clip 2 is a close-range architectural shot, not an overhead survey. Area-based park metrics are meaningless at that framing and were suppressed.
recommendations.Recommended action: Keep close-range structure footage as separate, clearly-labelled inspection clips - they are valuable as visual evidence but should not feed the park-wide percentages.

recommendations.Finding: No class exists for the defects that matter most here: paint failure, damp staining, cracked render, dustbins, streetlights, water coolers, monuments, water pipes.
recommendations.Recommended action: Paint and damp condition on vertical surfaces is a genuinely different problem from the ground-plane work done so far and would need its own approach. Confirm whether it is wanted.

recommendations.Finding: No .SRT telemetry accompanied these clips, and this is a single-date capture.
recommendations.Recommended action: Export flight logs with the video to unlock geo-tagging; repeat the flight path later for change detection against this baseline.
